scores.evidence: Phase 1: Tenant Isolation & Audit Validation ... Depends on: Phase 0 (V0 passes); V1, V3 (must pass before Phase 2 starts).
scores.rationale: Gated ordering (isolation/audit before invoicing, V-gates before next phase) is good, but webhooks come after processor integration and Phase 0 already includes webhook/processor stubs, and some gates like cost sit oddly.

scores.evidence: A single invoice generated end-to-end ... in production, deployed through CI/CD, monitored, and rolled back.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real thin end-to-end slice in prod behind a flag with rollback and exit checks.

scores.evidence: Default: Row-level security in shared schema ... Flip condition: V1 fails, or audit finds cross-tenant queries → switch to schema-per-tenant
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions have reversibility, default, assumption, validation and flip condition.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 tasks: Tenant isolation hardening ... then Audit schema hardening ... Cost baseline
scores.rationale: Broad-impact items (tenancy, audit) come early and gates precede leaf work, but within-phase ordering is not explicitly reasoned by blast radius.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Feature flag + allow-list + internal JWT (test service account). No real customer data.
scores.rationale: Security has concrete treatment in every phase from Phase 0 through Phase 5.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Log every API call (method, endpoint, tenant_id, HTTP status, latency). Sentry for errors. CloudWatch for logs.
scores.rationale: Observability present in Phase 0 and concretely in every later phase.

scores.evidence: CI/CD pipeline: lint → unit tests → staging deploy ... Commit hash tagged. Test data seeded in /var/dfa-data/phase-0-seed.sql.
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed per phase with pipelines, seeds, Ansible, fixtures, tagged releases.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Rollback: Feature flag off (1 min). Phase 2: Retry with exponential backoff; Phase 3: Chaos test
scores.rationale: Resilience appears concretely in every phase, from rollback in Phase 0 to retries, chaos tests, backups and gradual rollout.

scores.evidence: N/A — no AI component. The system does not use LLMs, RAG, fine-tuning, or agentic orchestration.
scores.rationale: Plan explicitly declares the AI layer not applicable and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Advanced proration rules ... Pull forward if: (a) customer demand > 10% of early cohort, or (b) revenue impact analysis shows ≥ 5% MRR
scores.rationale: Eight deferred items each have reasons and concrete pull-forward conditions.

note: Strong plan: real prod walking skeleton, concrete gates and flip conditions, per-phase threaded concerns and explicit deferrals; weaker on explicit blast-radius ordering and some dependency-order quirks.
